info.name: Garrison
info.description:
Garrison REST, A2A, and MCP APIs (v0.1.0-alpha).

Select the Garrison environment, start a server and a worker that has `garrison-fake-harness` on its PATH, and run the collection top to bottom. The Auth folder signs in and stores a session token that every later request uses; the folders in between create resources with unique names and exercise every route; Cleanup deletes them again. The last folder restarts the server, so leave it out against shared servers.

Environment variables: `baseUrl`, `mcpUrl`, `tenantId`, `email`, `password`, `adminApiKey`, `accessKey`, `secretKey`, `nodeAccessKey`, `nodeSecretKey`. Identifiers created along the way are stored as collection variables.

See REST_API.md, MCP_API.md, A2A_API.md, and WEBSOCKETS_API.md in the repository for the full reference.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Anonymous readiness check (same as /v1.0/api/health/ready). Answers 200 when the database answers, its schema is current, and the replica is not draining; 503 otherwise.

Always 200 while the process runs, including during migrations and draining. The same answer is served on the separate liveness port (Rest.LivenessPort, default 8702) from its own thread; point liveness probes there.
200 only when the database answers, the schema is current, and the replica is not draining. Use it as the readiness probe.

request.description: Version, endpoints (REST, MCP, A2A), feature flags, and `observability`: the Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, and Tempo URLs from the Observability.* cluster settings plus the Grafana datasource and dashboard UIDs, with null for anything not configured. Reachability and version of Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, and Tempo, checked by the server against the Observability.*InternalUrl settings (or the browser URLs). Always four entries in the order grafana, prometheus, loki, tempo; cached for 30 seconds. Any authenticated caller may read it.

Prometheus text exposition relayed from the metrics listener (9464), so kubectl port-forward and in-pod 127.0.0.1 scrapes work. No authentication. 503 when the Prometheus listener is off, 404 when Telemetry.ServeMetricsOnServicePort is false.
The administrator API key in `x-api-key` bypasses RBAC. Use it for bootstrapping and platform administration.
Authenticates every request with `x-access-key` and `x-secret-key` instead of a token.

Signs the request with HMAC-SHA256 so the secret key never crosses the wire. The pre-request script builds the canonical string (method, path, query, tenant, date, nonce, body hash) and sets `x-date`, `x-nonce`, and `x-signature`.

item.name: Conversations
item.description: A conversation is a multi-turn session with one agent. Each turn is a run; every turn after the first resumes the harness session the earlier turns built. Start one with `startConversation` on invoke, create run, or a deployment test, then send `conversationId` with each later turn.

request.description: Invokes the agent with `startConversation` set, which makes the run the first turn of a new conversation. The run's `conversationId` names the conversation and `conversationTurn` is 1. Omit both fields for a one-off run outside any conversation.

exec: var json = {}; try { json = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { }
pm.test('first turn of a new conversation', function () { pm.expect(json.conversationId).to.match(/^cnv_/); pm.expect(json.conversationTurn).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Sends the next turn with `conversationId`. The turn runs on the conversation's deployment and the harness resumes its session, preferring the node that holds the conversation's directories. A turn sent while the previous one is unfinished gets 409 `ConversationBusy`: turns are refused, not queued. Other 409 codes are `ConversationAgentMismatch`, `ConversationDeploymentMismatch`, and `ConversationDeploymentUnavailable`; an unknown conversation is 404. The same two fields work on `POST /runs` and on deployment tests.

pm.test('second turn of the same conversation', function () { pm.expect(json.conversationId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('conversationId')); pm.expect(json.conversationTurn).to.eql(2); });

item.name: Pipelines
item.description: Pipelines run agents as ordered stages on one request: each stage is an ordinary run of its agent, sees the earlier stages' results through its PipelineStage prompt template, and can wait for a person to approve, request changes, or reject. This folder creates a two-stage pipeline on the Postman agent, runs it through a revision and an approval, exercises cancel, retry, and the 409 cases, and deletes everything it made, so it must run before Cleanup deletes the agent. Definitions need Pipeline permissions, pipeline runs need PipelineRun, and stage reviews need Read or Update on Approval. Run tokens cannot use any of these routes. See docs/PIPELINES.md and the Pipelines section of REST_API.md.

request.description: Creates a pipeline with two stages on the Postman agent. Stages run in list order and get positions 1 and 2. The first stage pins the deployment so it can pass the run parameter format (parameters are checked against that deployment's allowedRunOverrides when the pipeline is saved) and requires a review with at most one revision. The second stage uses the agent's weighted deployment selection and may run twice when it fails. Needs Create on Pipeline.
